CHIEF COMPLAINT
Second opinion regarding right index finger injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Philip Gutierrez is a 50-year-old male presenting for a second opinion regarding his right index finger. He sustained a hyperextension injury to the right index finger during a motor vehicle accident in March 2026 when his vehicle was rear-ended multiple times. He reports being a passenger, felt two bumps that slung him forward and caused his right index finger to stretch backward. He describes pain since the injury, approximately three months ago, with persistent swelling. He is unable to make a fist and reports pain ranging from unbearable to severe with activities like driving. He has been seen by an orthopedist and occupational therapist and had an MRI obtained. He reports receiving conflicting information about treatment options regarding steroid injection. He is right-handed and works as an x-ray technician, necessitating use of his dominant hand. He attempted to use a splint hoping to straighten the finger. He denies diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports experiencing heart racing with dexamethasone. Reports itching with methylprednisolone. Reports sensation of tearing in finger with attempts at motion. Notes some numbness. Pain with passive and active finger flexion and extension.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Motor vehicle accident in March 2026 with right index finger hyperextension injury.

MEDICATIONS
Blood pressure medication (specific agent not specified).

ALLERGIES
Dexamethasone (causes heart to race).
Methylprednisolone (causes itching).

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as an x-ray technician. Right-handed. Drove himself to the appointment today.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Pleasant, cooperative, healthy male in no distress. Regular heart rate and rhythm. 2+ radial pulse. No swelling or bruising in palm over volar surface of index finger. Normal creases, slightly diminished over PIP of index finger compared to middle finger. Index finger rests in 10-degree PIP-flexed position. Discomfort with passive correction. Slight numbness noted during examination. Pain with PIP flexion and extension. All extensors intact. Collateral ligaments intact. Able to make fist. Four views of right hand x-ray: no bony abnormalities, joint congruency throughout all lesser digits on right hand, no soft tissue shadows of concern, no arthritis.

RESULTS
MRI (4/24/2021 from Point May Orthopedics): Focal soft tissue swelling over right index MCP joint. Partial-thickness tear of right FDS (flexor digitorum superficialis). Fluid consistent with tenosynovitis around FDP and FDS tendons. Radial and ulnar collateral ligaments of index MCP joint intact. MCP joint capsule intact. Extensor tendons intact.
X-rays today (4 views of right hand): No bony abnormalities. Joint congruency throughout all lesser digits on right hand. No soft tissue shadows of concern. No arthritis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Post-traumatic severe stenosing tenosynovitis of right index finger with partial-thickness tear of FDS tendon (noted as the least important of two flexor tendons; partial tear of one half of whole tendon). Significant scar tissue and inflammation around FDS tendon blocking excursion of other tendons.

Plan:
1. Steroid injection with betamethasone (Celestone) 1 cc and lidocaine 0.5 cc administered today. First injection attempt was withdrawn due to patient's dramatic and violent painful reaction. Second injection attempt performed successfully with minor palmar vein bleeding that was cleaned and bandaged.
2. Ice this evening.
3. Ibuprofen recommended.
4. Outpatient physical therapy once weekly for six weeks prescribed.
5. Goal is full active and passive range of motion with no restrictions.
6. Patient counseled to actively move finger and discontinue splint use (splint immobilizes rather than mobilizes).
7. Patient reassured that no harm was done to finger.
8. Expectation that injection will provide pain relief beginning in 3-5 days with further improvement over subsequent weeks.
9. May require repeat injection in future.
10. Patient cleared to drive.
